notes: Real public products only. GTINs are GTIN-13 (UPC-A padded with a leading zero).
No Open Food Facts ingredient text is stored here: only tags, flags and a sha256 prefix of the text seen at curation time.
product_truth = label_text adjudicated, then raised to 'contains' by openFDA undeclared-allergen recalls (R-RECALL).
label_text = what the printed label text declares under the documented rules; score extraction against this.
role 'eval_only' SKUs never enter the demo catalogue: warm-up and onboarding read role 'demo' only; the eval runner registers or replays eval-only SKUs itself.
recalls[] dates are openFDA's, as YYYY-MM-DD: report_date, recall_initiation_date and termination_date (null until terminated). FDA recall numbers start with H- or F-.
Target market(s) for the intake manifest; the jurisdiction module maps groups to market codes (UK:<group>, US:<group>).

fetched_meta.disclaimer: Do not rely on openFDA to make decisions regarding medical care. While we make every effort to ensure that data is accurate, you should assume all results are unvalidated. We may limit or otherwise restrict your access to the API in line with our Terms of Service.

openfda.licence: public domain / CC0; no FDA endorsement

label_rules.scope: Reference labels per allergen group (contains | may_contain | none; 'unscored' when the rules disagree). They are derived only from recall texts and the documented rules below, never typed by hand.

recall_rules.R-RECALL: An openFDA enforcement report whose reason_for_recall names an allergen as undeclared makes that group 'contains' in product_truth (regulator or lab ground truth). Matching uses RECALL_TERMS in scripts/curate-manifest.ts on the reason text from its first 'undeclared' onwards (whole reason if that finds nothing); plant milks and cocoa butter are not milk.
recall_rules.R-RECALL-COCONUT: A recall reason whose only tree-nut term is coconut is recorded as a rule-against-rule conflict and does not set tree_nut: coconut is not in FDA Q&A Edition 5 Table 1 (Jan 2025) and is not an Annex II nut.

text_rules.R-NAME: An ingredient name in the label text that the lexicon maps to a group (EN/DE/FR/IT/ES; statutory definitions: Reg. (EU) 1169/2011 Annex II, FD&C Act 201(qq), FDA Q&A Ed. 5) makes it 'contains'. Trap phrases are masked first per group (e.g. cocoa butter for milk, coconut and nutmeg for tree_nut, buckwheat for gluten).
text_rules.R-EMPH: An allergen emphasised in the ingredient list (Reg. (EU) 1169/2011 Art. 21(1)(b); rendered by Open Food Facts as _word_) makes it 'contains'.
text_rules.R-CONTAINS: A 'Contains:' statement (FD&C Act 403(w)(1)(A)) or its DE/FR/IT/ES equivalent makes the named groups 'contains'.
text_rules.R-PREC: A group named only inside a precautionary clause ('may contain', 'traces of', 'kann Spuren ... enthalten', 'peut contenir', 'può contenere', 'puede contener', 'made in a factory that...') is 'may_contain'.
text_rules.R-WHEAT-IS-GLUTEN: Wheat 'contains' implies gluten_cereal 'contains' (Annex II item 1 names wheat as a cereal containing gluten).
text_rules.boilerplate: Allergy-advice boilerplate (UK lines that refer the reader to the allergens printed in bold) and free-from claims (e.g. gluten-free) are masked before matching.

label_rules.second_pass: Pass B maps the Open Food Facts allergens_tags (contains) and traces_tags (may_contain); it has no wheat signal.

adjudication.ADJ-AGREE: Pass A and pass B agree.
adjudication.ADJ-TEXT-ONLY: Wheat: pass B has no wheat signal, so pass A stands.
adjudication.ADJ-TEXT-DECLARED: Text says contains via emphasis or a Contains statement, tags disagree: the label declaration governs.
adjudication.ADJ-TEXT-NAME: Text says contains via an ingredient name, tags disagree: the ingredient list governs.
adjudication.ADJ-TEXT-PRECAUTION: Text names the group only precautionarily, tags disagree: the label wording governs (may_contain).
adjudication.ADJ-TRAP: Tags say contains, the text names nothing for the group but holds a documented trap word for it (e.g. cocoa butter for milk): none.
adjudication.ADJ-DISPUTED: Tags say contains or may_contain and the text rules find nothing explainable (e.g. a precautionary statement printed outside the ingredient text): the group is unscored.

limits: Pass A is a rule-based reader; a lexicon gap shows up as ADJ-DISPUTED (unscored), not as a silent 'none'.

Recall-derived positives describe the product, not its printed label: an undeclared allergen is by definition absent from the label text, so extraction is scored against label_text and the recall check is scored separately.
Open Food Facts text is crowd-sourced and may lag the physical label.

scenario_notes.AS_OF_REPLAY: The curated page holds 10 openFDA reports dated after 2026-10-10 (all reported 2026-10-14). Only H-0011-2027 (Donutful) carries a UPC that resolves in Open Food Facts; the UPCs of H-0015-2027 (Queso Palmita, 0094922980045), H-0016-2027 and the four Saint Francis Apizza reports (H-0021..0024-2027) return 404, and H-0009, H-0017 and H-0025-2027 yield no check-digit-valid UPC. No SKU cleared before its recall exists, so the spec default (Donutful: HOLD on has_ingredients, then BLOCK after the poll) stands.
scenario_notes.E9: FSA-AA-48-2026 (Full On Flapjacks) has no Open Food Facts product (search.openfoodfacts.org brand query returned 0 hits), so its replay ends in 'no catalogue match' with the notice ingested. The name-only review path is shown by FSA-AA-45-2026 (Skinny Crunch, created 2026-10-13, inside the replay window) against 5056315500204, and by FSA-AA-44-2026 (Lambertz, 2026-10-03) against the two Lambertz SKUs.
scenario_notes.E8: Synthetic injection fixtures are eval-only and live with the guard tests, not in this manifest.
scenario_notes.E5: Derived from label_text for 5000169566558: contains [], may_contain [milk, tree_nut, peanut]. The precautionary statement names more groups than spec section 9.1's "May contain: milk", so the expected UK statement must list every may_contain group.
